entry.description:
Rule 210, the two-sided statement: no finite configuration keeps the period-2 clock on its center column. The primary source reports: For rule 210, $x' = \ell \oplus (\lnot c \wedge r)$, no finite configuration keeps the period-2 clock on its center column: if $x_0 : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ is white outside a bounded interval and $\mathrm{run210}\,x_0\,t\,0 = [t \text{ odd}]$ for every $t$, then false (`Rule30Submission.no_finite_clock`). Hence no finite configuration has an eventually alternating center column in either phase (`no_finite_eventually_alternating`), and the kit's seed does not (`seed_not_eventually_alternating`, through `run210_seed`).

The catalog's `Rule30ZeroBoundary.Q01` is the period-2 question for rule 30 in one-sided form, and `Rule30Realization.barrier` shows that rules 90, 150 and 210 share left-permutivity and Jen's theorem with rule 30. Our submission R30-20261022-920c1b showed the one-sided statement false for rule 210: the empty left half keeps the clock. This essay proves the two-sided statement true, so for rule 210 the finite-configuration form of period 2 holds while the zero-boundary form fails.

Under the clock every black cell of the left half has $t + k$ even (`parity_left_of_clock`), so the left half is parity-sparse and evolves as rule 90. Each admissible left row has a parity-sparse clock realization (`clock_bg`); a finite configuration either equals one, where rule 90's freshman's dream $x_{2^n} = x \oplus \sigma^{2^n} x$ breaks the clock at time $2^n + 1$ (`no_finite_clock90`), or first deviates from it at some depth, and a clearing front then carries the deviation to the center column at a computed time (`Dev.odd_impossible`, `Dev.even_impossible`).

Nothing is claimed about rule 30 itself, nor about infinite configurations of rule 210. entry.description:
The channel bound at width 14: explicit automaton states, one kernel check per state. The primary source reports: For every configuration $x : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ whose center column reads the clock, $\mathrm{evol}\,x\,t\,0 = [t \text{ odd}]$ for all $t$, the first $n$ visible bits $\mathrm{visFrom}\,x\,0\,n$ (column $1$ at the even times) lie in one set $S$ of words with $|S| \cdot 10^{9n} \le 300 \cdot 1184655442^{\,n}$ (`Rule30Submission.channel_bound_14`): about $0.2445$ bits of information per visible bit asymptotically ($\log_2(1184655442/10^9) \approx 0.24447$, with a finite correction $\log_2 300 / n$).

The catalog reduces period 2 to `Rule30ZeroBoundary.Q01` and has nothing about the right neighbour of a clocked column. Our submission R30-20261023-4767e0 proved this bound at width $12$ ($0.258$ bits) by rebuilding the window automaton inside one kernel computation; that does not scale, since the kernel's caches live for one declaration. Here the certificate is explicit: the bitset of each of the $919$ states of the width-$14$ automaton, its graph and Collatz-Wielandt weights.

One theorem per state (`s14_i`) has the kernel sweep the state's bitset and check that every member's four two-step images, with the cell beyond the window at the two successive times as free inputs, lie in the successor of its label (`stateCheck`); `explicit_sound` assembles the $919$ theorems into the closure of every edge, `bound_of` and `weight_bound` give the bound, and `win_step2` ties the window to the kit's `evol`. The sets are checked data, not derived: any family with the root full and every edge closed bounds the words.

Nothing here decides `Q01`: the bound measures the right neighbour. Width $16$ (about $0.2131$ bits) would need about $45$ MB of state literals in this form and is not attempted. For every configuration $x : \mathbb{Z} \to \mathrm{Bool}$ whose center column reads the clock, $\mathrm{evol}\,x\,t\,0 = [t \text{ odd}]$ for all $t$, the first $n$ visible bits $\mathrm{visFrom}\,x\,0\,n$ (column $1$ at the even times) lie in one set $S$ of words with $|S| \cdot 10^{9n} \le 300 \cdot 1184655442^{\,n}$ (`Rule30Submission.channel_bound_14`): about $0.2445$ bits of information per visible bit asymptotically ($\log_2(1184655442/10^9) \approx 0.24447$, with a finite correction $\log_2 300 / n$).

The catalog reduces period 2 to `Rule30ZeroBoundary.Q01` and has nothing about the right neighbour of a clocked column. Our submission R30-20261023-4767e0 proved this bound at width $12$ ($0.258$ bits) by rebuilding the window automaton inside one kernel computation; that does not scale, since the kernel's caches live for one declaration. Here the certificate is explicit: the bitset of each of the $919$ states of the width-$14$ automaton, its graph and Collatz-Wielandt weights.

One theorem per state (`s14_i`) has the kernel sweep the state's bitset and check that every member's four two-step images, with the cell beyond the window at the two successive times as free inputs, lie in the successor of its label (`stateCheck`); `explicit_sound` assembles the $919$ theorems into the closure of every edge, `bound_of` and `weight_bound` give the bound, and `win_step2` ties the window to the kit's `evol`. The sets are checked data, not derived: any family with the root full and every edge closed bounds the words.

Nothing here decides `Q01`: the bound measures the right neighbour. Width $16$ (about $0.2131$ bits) would need about $45$ MB of state literals in this form and is not attempted.

entry.description:
Two More Eventual Words Excluded from the Center Column of Rule 30. The primary source reports: For the single-seed evolution of rule 30, the center column is not eventually the repeating word $0^9\,1$, nor the repeating word $0^7\,1\,0\,1\,1$, whatever the transient and the phase: `Rule30Submission.not_eventually_0000000001` and `Rule30Submission.not_eventually_00000001011` prove `¬ EventuallyWord w` for these two words.

What is new: `Rule30StripCertificateTable` excludes thirty words of lengths 8 to 13, and `Rule30StripCertificates` the rank-certificate words $0^6\,1\,1$ and $0^9\,1\,0\,1$; neither word here is among them, in any rotation. `Rule30WhiteEnd` excludes $1\,0^q$ for every $q \ge 10$ and claims nothing for $q \le 9$; its `control_q9` shows that its check fails at $q = 9$. The first word is exactly that case.

Method: each proof is a rank certificate in the format of `Rule30StripCertificates.Cert` (strip width 12 with 40,010 ranks for the first word, width 6 with 552 ranks for the second), found by computer search and checked by the Lean kernel with `decide +kernel`. The kit's soundness theorem `Cert.not_eventuallyWord`, through masked Jen, gives the exclusion.

Nothing is claimed for the words $1\,0^q$ with $q \le 8$, for other words, or for Problem 1 itself. entry.description:
Sparse16: A Finite Obstruction to an Alternating Center in Rule 30. The primary source reports: For every Boolean half-line $L$, if the official zero-boundary Rule 30 evolution is black at depth 1 at all 56 even times $0,2,\ldots,110$, then at least 17 of $L(1),\ldots,L(111)$ are black. The farther initial tail is unrestricted. This is the theorem `Rule30Submission.PortableSparse16.fifty_six_even_black_forces_seventeen`. Its corollaries include an even white observation for every prefix of weight at most 16, and a necessary left-prefix weight for a whole-line configuration whose center alternates from time zero.

The primary source reports: The kit's Rule30ZeroBoundaryWidth52 proves that every zero-boundary start supported at depths at most 52 has a white depth-1 cell at some even time at most 96, and says of 96 that its tightness is observed, not proved. This essay proves the tightness: the explicit start 0x7dc2ff6fcc4fd is black at depth 1 at every even time below 96 and white at 96, by the kit's packed evaluator prun and its bridge run_toFun, so the death time at width 52 is exactly 96 (the headline theorem Rule30Submission.death_time_52_exact). Two further explicit starts give the lower bounds 100 at width 56 and 114 at width 60 (width56_lower, width60_lower); in our record both are exact by complete chunk certificates at K = 101 and K = 115, which are not carried here. The primary source reports: For the general left-permutive cellular automaton family `run (g : Bool -> Bool -> Bool)` in `Ruliology.CellularAutomata.Rule30Realization`, Jen's adjacent-column theorem `run_not_adjacent` assumes `g false false = false` and `g false true = true`. We prove that a Boolean function `g` satisfies these two hypotheses if and only if `g = g90 \lor g = g150 \lor g = g210 \lor g = g30` (`Rule30Submission.jen_class_iff_four_rules`). Within this four-element class, we prove three exact equivalences for the single-seed evolution `run g`: (1) `\forall t\,p,\, run g t p = run g90 t p` holds if and only if `g = g90 \lor g = g210` (`Rule30Submission.run_eq_run90_iff_g90_or_g210`); (2) the single-seed pattern is mirror-symmetric (`\forall t\,p,\, run g t (-p) = run g t p`) if and only if `g = g90 \lor g = g150 \lor g = g210` (`Rule30Submission.run_symm_iff_not_g30`); and (3) the center column `fun t => run g t 0` is not eventually constant (`\lnot \exists T\,b,\, \forall t \ge T,\, run g t 0 = b`) if and only if `g = g30` (`Rule30Submission.g30_unique_nonconstant_in_jen_class`).

entry.description: Telling left edges apart from the center column: exact deadlines for three edge pairs. The primary source reports: For any two configurations x, y of rule 30 whose leftmost black cells sit at -2 and -1, the center columns differ at some time t <= 8 (sep_8); for leftmost black cells at -4 and -3 by time 13 (sep_13), at -3 and -2 by time 14 (sep_14); each bound is attained (attained_8, attained_13, attained_14). The right side is unrestricted, finite or infinite. The kit's later module Rule30TraceEdge names the conjecture that two finite configurations with the same complete center trace have the same left edge and proves that it implies Problem 1; these are three exact negative-edge cases of the conjecture, for every configuration with those edges. The center through time m depends on the initial cells at positions at most m only, so a configuration is cut to the window [a, m]; the 2^(m - a) fillings with a black cell at a run as lanes of one number, the signatures of each edge class are collected into a bitset, and the bitsets are disjoint, checked by the kernel in blocks of 256 values. Nothing is claimed about the general conjecture or Problem 1. entry.description: Two infinite families of right halves absorbed by the ether: CQ01 for every right half with one of two prefixes. The primary source reports: The kit's coupled question CQ01 holds iff for every finite right half R the sideways row Psi R, the constrained start whose free bits complement column 1 of R driven by the alternating column, has infinitely many black cells; it holds for R whenever that column is eventually periodic (the kit's absorption route), and the milestone R = empty is open. For R31, black cells 1..5, and R495, black cells 1..4 and 6..9 (the row of R31 at time 4), the driven right half enters the kit's ether-and-wall trap: at time 9, respectively 5, columns 1..6 carry the kit's 7 x 4 ether with the alternating column as its column B4, and columns 7..19 are one of the kit's 109 wall states. Radius-one locality carries this entry to every right half that agrees with R31 on cells 1..28, or with R495 on cells 1..24, whatever its later cells, and the kit's trap invariant keeps the ether for ever, so all of them have the parity of the step as their visible column. Hence CQ01 for every finite member of the two families (CQ01_prefix31, CQ01_prefix495), among them the pairwise distinct right halves R31 plus one black cell at 29 + n (CQ01_fam, fam_injective), all with one sideways row (Psi_prefix31, Psi_prefix495, Psi_eq). The seeds are not joined by the right-end moves, the inverse of the kit's terminal rewrites 011 -> 01 and 101 -> 11 (not_move_equivalent). Nothing is claimed about CQ01 in general, the empty right half, or Problem 1. entry.description: A three-fifths bound on black runs in the rule 30 center column. The primary source reports: We prove in Lean that a black run of the rule 30 center column lasts at most about three fifths of its starting time: if c(a) = … = c(a + L − 1) = 1 with a ≥ 1, then L ≤ a − 2⌊(a − 1)/5⌋, hence 5L ≤ 3a + 10 (headline `Rule30Submission.black_run_three_fifths`). The kit's catalog had L ≤ a (`Rule30CenterRuns.black_run_le`). As consequences, every window [a, (8a + 10)/5] contains a white cell, so there are about log_{8/5} n white cells before time n, where the catalog had ⌊log₄ n⌋; the argument also bounds alternating blocks anywhere in the light cone and, relative to the first black cell right of the center, white runs. Under a black run the row at time a alternates. Going back in time, left-permutivity rebuilds each earlier row from the later one and two unknown cells; whatever those cells are, the alternation heals four cells further out, so after s steps the row alternates on cells 4s to L − 1 + s left of the center. After ⌊(a − 1)/5⌋ steps this block would contain the two adjacent black cells of the left edge, which is impossible. The four-cell healing is in `Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripe.agrees_pre`; what is new is its use on a finite block together with the left edge. We claim no unconditional bound of slope below 1 for white runs, and nothing sublinear: 3/5 is the limit of this method. entry.description:

entry.description:
Unconditional Six-Cell and Seven-Cell Stripe-Tail Mortality and Sparse Return-Map Completion of (97, 0) in Zero-Boundary Rule 30. The primary source reports: We extend the zero-boundary stripe-prefix mortality hierarchy in WolframInstitute/Rule30PrizeKit from five tail cells (`v : Fin 32`, 64 classes) to all six-cell (`v : Fin 64`, 128 classes) and seven-cell (`v : Fin 128`, 256 classes) stripe-prefix tails in core Lean 4.35.0:

1. Variable-Width Front-Window Compression (15.5x orbit reduction): Certifying each non-exceptional front window `(w, 0)` at its minimal valid width `K in [8, 30]` (`S = K - 1 <= 29 < 31`) reduces the 16 six-cell front windows (`cyc6_33`..`cyc6_63` in `Rule30Certificates/ZeroBoundaryStripeCycles4`) from 589,824 steps at `K = 32` to 62,848 steps (6.11 s, 0.28 GB RSS), and the 31 non-exceptional seven-cell front windows (`cyc7_65`..`cyc7_127`, `w != 97`, in `Rule30Certificates/ZeroBoundaryStripeCycles5`) from 1,179,648 steps to 51,008 steps (5.29 s, 0.27 GB RSS).

2. Discovery and Completion of `(97, 0)`: Across all odd front windows up to 7 bits (`w in 1..127`), `(97, 0)` is the unique new window after `(13, 0)` that fails to close at `K <= 34`. We prove its width-26 punctured cycle (`L = 8,192`, single bad odd index `b = 6,313`) and lift it across a 32-state parallel upper return map at width 36, horizon 35 to `cycle97_complete : Cycle 36 35 97 0 262144` (`Rule30Certificates/StripeTail97Completion`, 11.16 s, 0.93 GB RSS).

3. Unconditional Horizon-45 Mortality (`Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripeSixSeven`, 8.15 s, 0.44 GB RSS): Combining these certificates with `cycle13_complete` establishes `stripe_six_tail` (125 classes at horizon 31), `stripe_six_tail_complete` (all 128 six-cell classes at horizon 45, `d <= m + 8`), `stripe_seven_tail` (251 classes at horizon 31), and `stripe_seven_tail_complete` (all 256 seven-cell classes at horizon 45, `d <= m + 9`).

entry.description: Least Period 4 of Rule 30: a Weaker Sufficient Condition, and Why the Left Half Must Be Finite. The primary source reports: Problem 1 asks whether the center column of rule 30 is ever eventually periodic. The kit reduces the three words of least period 4 (0001, 0011, 0111) to the open statement Absorption (Rule30Ether): every finite right half driven by the word must eventually enter a family of ether-and-wall states. The kit's proof only uses a consequence of that entry, which we isolate as Lock w: every finite right half driven by w^∞ has column 1 eventually periodic at the white times of the driver (with any period 4Q), or some column q ≥ 1 eventually periodic. We prove in Lean that Lock w excludes w^∞ as a tail of the center column whatever the transient (Rule30Submission.lock_excludes, by masked Jen or by Jen), that the kit's Absorption implies Lock (lock_of_absorption), and that the three locks exclude least period 4 (least_period_four_of_lock). Lock is open for the three words, but it no longer mentions the ether, the wall or any entry state. Second, the proof uses the finiteness of the left half (through Jen), and that hypothesis cannot be weakened to spatial periodicity, even with a finite right half: for each of the three words, and for the alternating column 1, 0, 1, 0, …, there is a configuration whose left half is the 7-periodic ether and whose right half is finite (ether columns, one of the kit's wall states, then white), with center column exactly the word from time 0 (period_four_left_periodic_right_finite, alt_left_periodic_right_finite). The kit's ether_coupled_witness had both halves infinite. Numerically, every right half of width ≤ 24 locks for the three words, the locking time does not depend on the width, and among the words of period ≤ 7 these three are the only ones whose driven right halves locked for every finite right half we tested, so Lock is a statement about period 4 only. entry.description: Rule 30, Period 2: a Closed Trap for the Right Half Driven from the Empty Row. The primary source reports: Problem 1 asks whether the center column of rule 30 is ever eventually periodic. For period 2 the kit has the coupled question CQ01 (no configuration with finitely many black cells has center column 1, 0, 1, 0, … from time 0): for every finite right half R there is exactly one candidate left row Psi R, whose free bits are the complement of u R, column 1 of the right half R driven by the alternating column, read at the white steps; CQ01 holds iff Psi R is infinite for every finite R, and the milestone CQ01Empty, the case R = ∅, is open. We prove in Lean that u ∅ follows the ether (gaps 2 and 5) and then, from s = 146 on and for ever, has gaps 3 or 5 between consecutive black cells (Rule30Submission.u_empty_gaps): the windows of columns 1..16 at the odd steps form a set of 829 windows that is closed under the double step whatever column 17 does, and inside it the gaps are 3 or 5 (kernel checks), and the window of R = ∅ enters it at step 293. The same holds for every right half whose window enters the trap (gaps_of_entry); numerically 96 % of random finite right halves enter it, and the others have u eventually periodic, a case the kit already settles. Spacing 3 or 5 of such a gate is the hypothesis that the kit's recent modules on gates assume without claiming it for any finite right half; we prove it for R = ∅ from s = 146 on (`u_empty_window` for `Rule30DrivenPrefix.Window`, `u_empty_spaced` for `Rule30SpacingRenormalization.Spaced`), and that the transformed gate is not spaced, so their eight-column translation cannot be iterated on it (`u_empty_transform_not_spaced`). This turns CQ01Empty into a left-only statement weaker than the kit's Q01: Q01Gap, no finitely supported constrained start of the zero-boundary left half has free bits that are eventually the complement of a concatenation of 001 and 00001. We prove Q01 ⇒ Q01Gap, Q01Gap ⇒ ¬ FinSupp (Psi R) for every R entering the trap (not_finSupp_Psi_of_Q01Gap), hence Q01Gap ⇒ CQ01Empty (CQ01Empty_of_Q01Gap). Q01Gap is open; nothing here excludes period 2. entry.description: Rule 30: Self-Shielded Black Runs, Sharper White-Run Bounds, and Q01 as an Integer Iteration. The primary source reports: Problem 1 asks whether the center column of rule 30 is ever eventually periodic. We prove three partial results in Lean, against the current kit. **Self-shielding.** By the kit's Lemma A* (`Rule30BlackRuns.black_shield`), a black run of length 9j in the center column forces the pattern (white, black)^j in columns 1..2j. This pattern shields itself: it moves two columns to the right every two steps without reading the cell on its right, so for 2j steps after the run the columns 1..2j depend only on the center column, and column 1 is determined for 4j steps instead of the 2j of the light cone. With masked Jen this halves the slope of the kit's Theorems B and D: if the center column is eventually P-periodic, it has no black run of length r < P followed by a white cell with 9⌈(P−r)/4⌉ ≤ r (`Rule30Submission.no_long_black_run_quarter`; the kit needs 9⌈(P−r+9)/2⌉ ≤ r), and similarly for a black run followed by a white run (`no_black_white_run_quarter`). So every word 1^r u with 1 ≤ |u| ≤ 4 and u starting white is excluded for r ≥ 9 (`no_black_run_ge9_len_le4`; the kit's `Rule30BlackRunBlocks` needs r ≥ 18 or 27 for its eight blocks), and every 1^r u with |u| ≤ 8 for r ≥ 18. **White runs.** Theorem W′ (`no_white_run_block`) excludes 0^r (1 :: v) as the eventual period from two finite kernel-checked certificates. It gives eight tails with sharper bounds than the catalog: r ≥ 12 for 1011, 10011, 11011, 101011 and 110011, r ≥ 20 for 111001, r ≥ 21 for 100011 and 111011 (the catalog: 49, 61 or 71). **An integer form of Q01.** One step of the kit's zero-boundary left half, read as a binary number, is F(Y) = ⌊Y/2⌋ XOR (Y OR 2Y), and the kit's open condition Q01, which excludes period 2, holds iff every natural number Y reaches an even number under some iterate of G = F∘F (`Q01_iff_integer`). F is tied to the kit's moving-frame map Φ(Y) = Y XOR (2Y OR 4Y) by Φ(Y) = 2F(Y) + (Y mod 2). Numerically every Y < 2^16 reaches an even number within 16 steps of G. None of this excludes period 2, 3 or 4: their words have no black run of length 9, and Q01 stays open. Left-Diagonal Defect Spectra, Sublinear Monochromatic Run Bounds, and Semigroup Saturation in Rule 30. The primary source reports: This submission presents Emerson Villafuerte's verified work on diagonal defect spectra and run bounds across 88 kernel-verified theorems.

Key results and clarifications:
1. Universal Black Run Bound: for all a >= 4, every black run on the center column satisfies L <= a - 2 (`black_run_center_le_ge4`), strictly improving Morales's linear bound L <= a. As noted in peer review, this bound is strictly stronger than the three-fifths bound of R30-20261025-0554f7 (L <= a - 2 Floor[(a - 1)/5]) at a = 4 (2 < 4) and a = 5 (3 < 5).
2. Recurrence Window: every interval [a, 2a - 2] holds a white cell (`exists_white_ge4`), contracting Morales's [a, 2a].
3. Conditional White Row Bound: diagonal defect theorems establish conditional bounds on alternating triangular preRow row blocks (`white_run_le_diag5`: L <= a - 5 whenever ell + 7 <= a). Per reviewer guidance, this is not an unconditional bound on center-column white runs, for which no bound L <= a - 5 holds since c(6) = c(7) = 0.
4. Diagonal Defect Spectrum: exact closed-form period determinations D_2(t+2) = false, D_3(t+2) = [t = 1 mod 2], D_4(t+2) = true, and D_5(t+3) = [t = 0 mod 2], with defect theorems bounding runs by a - j.

entry.description:
Partial structural results toward Rule 30 Problem 1: a truncation bridge, first kernel-checked Q001 instances, and a coupled golden-mean source constraint. The primary source reports: **Result.** Partial results toward Problem 1, via the kit's left-half reductions `Q01` (period 2) and `Q001` (least period 3). A generic truncation bridge, `constrained_black_window`: a width-$d$ death bound $D$ forces a black cell at a depth in $(d, D+1]$ in *every* row whose column $-1$ matches a fixed pattern on a time-set forever  finite or infinite rows alike. Instances: `black_window_52` (a black cell in $(d, 97]$ for every $d \le 52$) and the period-3 `q001_black_window`. The first kernel-checked instances of `Q001`: `q001_cases_up_to_16`, `q001_width_le_16`. An equivalence upgrade, `q001_iff_finite_dies`: `Q001` holds iff every finitely supported zero-boundary start has column $-1$ white at some step $3j$. A coupled structural constraint: `no_two_by_two_black` (Rule 30 has no $2\times 2$ all-black block) and `source_no_vertical_11` (the adjacent-black source is $11$-free in time).

**New relative to the catalog.** The kit has no kernel-checked `Q001` instances (its evidence is a non-kernel C search); the truncation-bridge and black-window statements, and the coupled adjacent-black-source ($11$-free) structure, are absent from the catalog.

**Method.** Left-permutivity (the OR-latch $x_i = 1 \Rightarrow F(x)_i = x_{i-1} \oplus 1$) gives the no-$2\times2$ / $11$-free source in three lines. Triangular truncation turns any width-$d$ kernel death bound into an unconditional black-window statement for infinite constrained rows; the `Q001` instances are kernel-checked finite case analyses; `adjSrc_factor_le_fib` uses the elementary count of $11$-free words, $\mathrm{fib}(n+2)$.

**Not claimed.** No prize problem is solved; Problems 1-3 remain open. These are partial results toward the `Q01` / `Q001` reductions, not a proof of non-periodicity. The $\mathrm{fib}(n+2)$ factor-complexity bound is elementary and orthogonal to the prize: an upper bound on a *derived* sequence, whereas Problem 1 needs an unbounded *lower* bound on the center column itself. challengeContext.anchorClaim:
The source reports: **Result.** Partial results toward Problem 1, via the kit's left-half reductions `Q01` (period 2) and `Q001` (least period 3). A generic truncation bridge, `constrained_black_window`: a width-$d$ death bound $D$ forces a black cell at a depth in $(d, D+1]$ in *every* row whose column $-1$ matches a fixed pattern on a time-set forever  finite or infinite rows alike. Instances: `black_window_52` (a black cell in $(d, 97]$ for every $d \le 52$) and the period-3 `q001_black_window`. The first kernel-checked instances of `Q001`: `q001_cases_up_to_16`, `q001_width_le_16`. An equivalence upgrade, `q001_iff_finite_dies`: `Q001` holds iff every finitely supported zero-boundary start has column $-1$ white at some step $3j$. A coupled structural constraint: `no_two_by_two_black` (Rule 30 has no $2\times 2$ all-black block) and `source_no_vertical_11` (the adjacent-black source is $11$-free in time).

**New relative to the catalog.** The kit has no kernel-checked `Q001` instances (its evidence is a non-kernel C search); the truncation-bridge and black-window statements, and the coupled adjacent-black-source ($11$-free) structure, are absent from the catalog.

**Method.** Left-permutivity (the OR-latch $x_i = 1 \Rightarrow F(x)_i = x_{i-1} \oplus 1$) gives the no-$2\times2$ / $11$-free source in three lines. Triangular truncation turns any width-$d$ kernel death bound into an unconditional black-window statement for infinite constrained rows; the `Q001` instances are kernel-checked finite case analyses; `adjSrc_factor_le_fib` uses the elementary count of $11$-free words, $\mathrm{fib}(n+2)$.

**Not claimed.** No prize problem is solved; Problems 1-3 remain open. These are partial results toward the `Q01` / `Q001` reductions, not a proof of non-periodicity. The $\mathrm{fib}(n+2)$ factor-complexity bound is elementary and orthogonal to the prize: an upper bound on a *derived* sequence, whereas Problem 1 needs an unbounded *lower* bound on the center column itself.

Correction: this replaces R30-20261022-5c4fbf, which counted all 48 words as new. Nine were excluded before it: `0 1^14` and `0 1^15` in every column (`Rule30FiniteBlackRuns`); `0^12 1 1`, `0^13 1 1` and `0^14 1 1` for every nonzero finite configuration (`Rule30WhiteRunEight`, `Rule30FiniteWhiteRuns`); `0^9 1 0 1` for the single seed (`Rule30StripCertificates`); and `1 0^13` to `1 0^15` by our R30-20261022-c27323. So 39 words are new, and for four more only the statement for every configuration with a leftmost black cell is new. The Lean is unchanged apart from its docstring. The argument is Jen's, word by word: the K cells right of the column form a finite relaxation; after a few periods of the word, one more period maps its reachable set into itself while the next column takes a single value at every tick, so two adjacent columns are periodic, which the moving left edge forbids. entry.description: Periodic temporal profiles of rule 30: pulse holes, source weights and rooted returns. The primary source reports: We study Boolean temporal profiles related by the rule 30 left-diagonal recurrence C(t+1) = A(t) XOR (B(t) OR C(t)). `Rule30Submission.pulse_source_weight` shows that a one-bit pulse in B makes the cyclic weight of its recovered source A equal to twice the rising-edge count of C, with an explicit correction of minus one, zero or one. `Rule30Submission.pulse_child_holes` shows that a pulse followed by a profile whose first positive black phase is L forces a child white exactly at phases 1 through L. For q-periodic profiles with q at least 4, `Rule30Submission.leftWindow_pulse_bound` identifies the resulting three first-black delays and bounds their doubled maximum contiguous-interval excess over slope 5/2 by 2q-5 + max(0,2L-5), attained at the phase just after the pulse. Separately, `Rule30Submission.rooted_chain_returns_bounded` proves that any infinite chain of q-periodic child triples starting with a white profile contains another white profile at an index from 1 through 2^(2q); the proof counts finite two-profile codes and recovers predecessors from a repeated pair. Reset existence and uniqueness (`Rule30Submission.child_exists`, `Rule30Submission.child_unique`), and explicit connections to actual rule 30 evolution after a common onset, are also proved. These are conditional profile statements. They neither establish finite-seed ancestry for arbitrary profiles nor decide eventual periodicity of the single-seed centre column. entry.description: An explicit finite horizon for mechanical words beside a Rule 30 clock. The primary source reports: For every real slope alpha, phase theta and natural C, the mechanical word floor(theta+(s+1)alpha)-floor(theta+s alpha) has a repetition of positive lag q on [a,b] with b > 2a+q+C and b+q <= 251(C+4). Every recoding by a block map of width w+1 has one by 251(C+4)+250w. Suppose a Rule 30 row is white left of -L and column 0 alternates white and black from time 0. Then any stretch [a,b] of the visible neighbour x(1,2s) that agrees with such a recoded word has b-a < 251(L+2a+4)+250w, so reset times obey t' <= 503t+251L+1004+250w. The qualitative obstruction is classical, and finite continued-fraction estimates exist (Bugeaud-Kim); we claim neither priority nor sharpness. This is a checked quantitative bound with explicit Rule 30 endpoints. No density, realizability or prize result is claimed. entry.description:
An All-Time Forbidden Return-Gap Pattern in the Alternating-Driven Rule 30 Right Orbit. The primary source reports: We prove an all-time restriction on a driven subsystem that arises in the period-two case of Problem 1. Let `u R1` be the kit's sideways observation (`Rule30PeriodTwoSideways.u`) of the right half whose center boundary is driven by the alternating sequence $1,0,1,0,\ldots$, started from the right seed black only at position 1. Record the first-return gaps between consecutive black observations. Every gap is 3 or 5, the first three gaps are 5, and the gap sequence contains the factor $3,5,3,5,3,5,3$ at no index (`Rule30Submission.alternating_R1_no_3535353`). The factors $3,3$ and $3,5,5,3$ are excluded at every index as well.

Relative to the kit catalog and earlier submissions, which give eventual 3/5 spacing for the empty right seed and finite-window obstructions for an alternating center, the new content is the all-index exclusion of this seven-gap word for the one-cell right seed. The exclusions of $3,3$ and $3,5,5,3$ come from our earlier work and are not claimed as new.

Method: the odd-time driven right half is projected to an 18-cell window whose two unseen outer inputs are left free, giving a finite nondeterministic relaxation. A 2,040-state inductive invariant pool, 3,010 first-return edges, a 30-subset deterministic reader and a nine-state monitor show that no relaxed history realizes a forbidden factor; the kit's packed-prefix theorems transfer this to the actual orbit.

Not claimed: nonperiodicity of the free center column, $\neg\,\mathrm{FinSupp}(\Psi\,R_1)$, exclusion of eventual period two, or a solution of any Prize problem. The Universal Backward Wave Cascade, Clone-Ray Disjointness, and 16-Ray All-Length Mortality for Zero-Boundary Stripe Prefixes. The primary source reports: Building on `Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripeStructure` and `Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripePrimitiveRoots`, we formalize `Rule30ZeroBoundaryStripeCascade` in core Lean 4.35.0 (~5.0 s, zero certificate tables):

1. The Universal 4-Stage Backward Wave Cascade (`bstep1_nor_period_three`, `typeI_step3_nor_wave`, `typeI_eight_bit_three_phases`, `wave_100_to_011_step1`, `wave_100_to_011_step0`, `wave_011_to_period6_step0`): Whenever `V.testBit i = true` for `i >= m`, `X = bstep1 K V` obeys the NOR recurrence `X_i = !(X_{i-1} || X_{i-2})` and locks into a period-3 `(100)^infty` wave. Thus every Type I primitive root enters the period-3 `(100)^infty` wave at backward step 3 (`bstep1 K (B_shift K W)`), with the three 8-bit Type I roots `201, 225, 253` realizing all three wave phases. One further backward step (`bstep1 K` or `bstep0 K`) maps any `(100)^infty` wave to its bitwise complement `(011)^infty` (period 3), and the next step (`bstep0 K`) doubles the spatial period from 3 to 6, locking into `(000101)^infty` (`wave_011_to_period6_step0`).
2. Global Injectivity of `F_shift` & Disjoint Clone Rays (`F_shift_injective`, `B_shiftIter_F_shiftIter`, `clone_ray_disjoint_of_primRoot`): `F_shift` is globally injective on `Nat`, iterated backward reduction `B_shiftIter j K` recovers any root `W` from `F_shiftIter j W`, and clone rays generated by primitive roots `W_1, W_2` intersect at `(j_1, j_2)` iff `j_1 = j_2 /\ W_1 = W_2`.
3. Canonical Stripe-Prefix Defect Absorption & 16-Ray All-Length Mortality (`rowTail_absorb_stripe`, `rowTail_fifteen_rays_31`, `rowTail_sixteen_rays_all_odd`): Absorbing `d` stripe-matching bits into the prefix gives `rowTail m w = rowTail (m + d) (w >>> d)`. entry.description: The death time at width 60 is exactly 114: a complete chunk certificate and its witness. The primary source reports: The kit proves Q01 for every zero-boundary start of width at most 52 by 256 kernel-decided chunk checks with the bound 96. This module carries 4,096 checks at width 60 at K = 115, assembled by the kit's q01_of_chunks into q01_width_le_60 (every start of width at most 60 has a white depth-1 cell at an even time at most 114), and proves the bound exact: the explicit start 0xe77a4e77b8f99b5 is black at depth 1 at every even time below 114 and white at 114, by the kit's packed evaluator prun and its bridge run_toFun (the headline theorem Rule30Submission.death_time_60_exact).
